entries.test: Public audits of AI-assisted scientific work measuring substantive errors and establishing whether LLM hallucinations caused a significant share of that work to be wrong.

entries.test: Public reporting and studies documenting the prevalence of low-quality AI-generated material across journalism, law, music, politics, education, and other domains by August 2025.
entries.note: “Everywhere” has a plain contextual reading of widespread presence across domains, rather than literal universal coverage.
He quotes and reaffirms his own earlier argument. The normalization weakens “would go to zero” to “could”; the overarching threat claim nevertheless remains explicitly tentative.

entries.test: Public comparative studies and deployment evidence showing whether increased AI scale caused greater production or dissemination of erroneous and low-quality AI content by August 2025.
entries.note: The surrounding discussion gives “enshittification” a concrete referent in unreliable and low-quality AI-generated material.

entries.test: Public evidence of the spread of low-quality AI-generated material across domains and its documented harms by August 2025.
entries.note: The third-person closing is Marcus's own voice. In context, seriousness and ubiquity assert substantial harm and widespread presence.
